_comment: Overhead two-handed axe chop from a side-view sprite facing right: two key poses (wind-up, hit) painted on a padded canvas, a pause to approve them, then animate_image between them. A 256x256 canvas gives a long haft room and caps the clip at 8 generated frames.
_comment_prompt: /pixellab-pip run the overhead-axe-chop blueprint on hero.png

TASK.instruction: Before any PixelLab call, require an explicit current-user request to run this blueprint, confirm an authenticated PixelLab MCP connection, and create the declared output directory empty (lowest free -2 suffix if taken). Copy {{standing sprite}} in as standing.png; it must face right. Paste it unscaled onto a transparent {{canvas width | default: 256}}x{{canvas height | default: 256}} canvas at x={{pad x | default: 72}} with its lowest drawn row on the bottom edge (assets/pad_sprite.py does this), save padded.png and record the paste offset in pad.json. Stop if the sprite does not fit, the canvas breaks the animate_image limit (width x height x 8 <= 524288, at most 256 per side), or any check fails. Resolve current-request overrides before execution; the blueprint is a recipe, not permission. Follow the canonical approval and content-review contracts in references/auto.md and references/reviewable-candidates.md. The user must accept any proposed local pixel/playback transformations separately from spending approval.
TASK.verify: padded.png has the canvas size, every opaque pixel equals standing.png at the recorded offset, and the output folder is new and inside the project.

MCP edit_image_pro_flash.description: The same {{character description}}, wind-up of an overhead chop: holding one {{weapon | default: two-handed greataxe}} with both hands together at the end of the haft over the shoulder, the axe head up behind the head, edge facing up toward the upper left of the image, torso arched back, very long stride, front knee bent, back leg straight. The same axe head, same size, the haft as long as in the original. Same size, same colours and pixel style, feet in the same place, no background.

TASK.instruction: Poll MCP get_image with the job_id returned by the immediately preceding call until completed or failed; re-poll on transient errors and never resubmit. Save the image unchanged as keys/key-a.png.
TASK.verify: keys/key-a.png is a transparent PNG with the same dimensions as padded.png.

MCP edit_image_pro_flash.description: The same {{character description}}, the hit of an overhead chop: torso folded forward over the deep front knee, both arms extended low in front, holding one {{weapon | default: two-handed greataxe}}, the axe head at knee height in front, edge facing toward the lower right of the image, back heel lifted. The same axe head, same size, the haft as long as in the original. Same size, same colours and pixel style, feet in the same place, no background.

TASK.instruction: Poll MCP get_image for the immediately preceding job as above and save the image unchanged as keys/key-b.png. Show standing.png, key-a.png and key-b.png side by side at 3x and run the look checklist in references/characters.md: one axe, both hands on the haft and joined to the arms, the edge direction as described, head size and haft length match the standing sprite, nothing touches the canvas edge. Report the look result. Continue to interpolation only after this content checkpoint is approved, or when the current user explicitly delegated review of these exact key poses and they pass that review. Otherwise ask whether to animate the next already-approved calls or correct a pose. Any paid correction must fit an expressly approved retry scope or receive new spending approval.
TASK.verify: Both key poses exist at the padded size, the look check was reported, and continuation has approved or explicitly delegated content review.

MCP animate_image.action: brings the raised axe over the head and down in front in one heavy fast chop, folding forward into the deep lunge

TASK.instruction: Poll MCP get_image for the immediately preceding job until completed or failed; never resubmit. Save all returned images unchanged in order as frames/frame-00.png onward; frame-00 is the echoed first frame. Run the animation doctor with --check-only (references/animation-doctor.md) on the frames with padded.png as the reference and the first and last frames marked as approved key poses, writing into doctor/ only, and report its verdict and look list without changing any source frame.
TASK.verify: Nine readable transparent frames of identical size are saved in returned order, the doctor report exists, and no source frame was modified.

TASK.instruction: Assemble frame-00 through frame-08 in order, without resizing or repainting, into final/axe-chop.png as one row with final/axe-chop.json in Aseprite sheet format (assets/make_sheet.py), with per-frame durations {{frame durations | default: 160 ms on frame 0, 140 ms on the last contact frame, 60 ms otherwise}}, the pad offset from pad.json, facing right and the hit frame index. Write final/axe-chop.gif as a labeled looping preview with those delays using assets/preview_gif.py. Decode and compare count, order, alpha and representable timing with the source PNGs; stop and report a GIF representation limit rather than silently quantizing colours, alpha or timing. If the user requires a play-once artifact, use an available supported export that preserves that behavior or report the limitation before delivering; the standard preview helper always loops.
TASK.verify: The sheet has nine cells matching their sources pixel-for-pixel, timing lives only in durations (no duplicated frames), and the decoded GIF preserves representable source pixels, frame count/order and timing, or its limit is reported.
